newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close higher, Telkom sharply up.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close higher, Telkom sharply up.

text.p: Jakarta shares closed higher on Tuesday, boosted by an increase in the price of market heavyweight Telkom and active buying of some secondaries, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index rose 5.56 points, or 0.96 percent, to close at 583.87 points after touching a high for the day of 584.14 in late trade. Gainers led losers by 52 to 41, with 59 counters unchanged.
Brokers said the index was likely to stay in positive territory on Wednesday with possible foreign interest in a few medium and big-capitalised stocks.
Brokers said the sharp rise of the market's biggest capitalised stock Telkom had helped boost the index and led to some fresh buying in the afternoon session.
Telkom rose 150 rupiah to 3,750 on a turnover of 3.1 million shares. Brokers attributed the gains to Telkom's increase in New York on Monday coupled with speculation of improved nine-month results.

"But I think it's also due to government support ahead of the listing of BNI...I believe the government has an interest in keeping the prices of all state-dominated firms stable," said a broker from a London-based firm.
Brokers said overall trading volume was up from Monday despite the public offer of Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI). The BNI floatation has slowed trade on the Jakarta exchange for the last week.
BNI is floating 1.085 billion shares at 850 rupiah each during the four-day official offer period which ends on Thursday. It will be listed on the Jakarta and Surabaya exchanges on November 25.
Some bank stocks including Bank International Indonesia (BII), BDNI and Bank Surya were actively traded following the public offer of BNI, brokers said.

They said sentiment towards bank stocks had improved since following the BNI offer. "It is proving difficult to get as much BNI stock as we want, so we are moving into other bank stocks," a local broker said.
Bank International Indonesia traded unchanged at 2,200 rupiah on a volume of 3.9 million shares after touching 2,225 rupiah.
"Active buying of BII is due to its recent stock split and also the public offer of BNI," a local broker said.
Feedmill producer Anwar Sierad topped the active list with 6.2 million shares, up 150 rupiah to 2,525 rupiah.
Brokers said this was due to speculation that the firm's subsidiary Sierad Produce would soon be listed.

Toll road operator Citra Marga rose 75 rupiah to 1,850 on a volume of 3.1 million shares. Brokers said it was due to perception that its prevailing price was relatively low while the firm had good fundamentals.
